transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um, well, I've been having some issues with eating lately. What really made me come in is that once I start eating a lot, it feels like I hit some kind of switch. I just keep going, even while a part of me is thinking, you know, Dennis, just stop already. I just can't seem to stop myself once I start.

After these episodes where you feel unable to stop eating, do you do anything to try to make up for or counteract what you ate, such as making yourself throw up, taking laxatives, or exercising excessively?

No, I don't do any of that. I've never made myself throw up or taken laxatives or anything like that. And I definitely don't exercise to try and work it off. I usually just... I just kind of sit there feeling really full and awful about what I just did, but I don't do anything to try and undo it.
Did this pattern of overeating start after a particular stressful event or major life change?
Yeah, I guess it did. It started right around the time I moved into my off-campus apartment. That was about five months ago, so it's been going on for about that long.
Do you find that you typically overeat in response to feeling stressed, upset, or overwhelmed, as a way to comfort yourself?

I don't think so. Um, I mean, I definitely get stressed with classes and everything, but I wouldn't say I eat because I'm upset or trying to comfort myself. I haven't really noticed a connection like that. It just kind of happens regardless of how I'm feeling.
About how often do these episodes of overeating happen in a typical week?

Well, since early in the semester, it’s been happening most weeks. Usually it's just one night a week. Sometimes it might be two nights, like if I have a bunch of deadlines or if there's just a lot of food piled up in the apartment. But yeah, I’d say that pattern has been pretty steady for at least the last three or four months.

inference_history.note: Patient presents with uncontrolled binge eating episodes, raising suspicion for eating disorders such as bulimia nervosa, binge-eating disorder (classified under other eating disorders), or anorexia nervosa.

Ruled out F50.2 and F50.0/F50.3 due to the absence of compensatory behaviors and pattern characteristic of binge eating without purging/restriction; added F50.4 (overeating associated with other psychological disturbances) and retained F50.8 (which includes binge eating disorder in ICD-10) and F50.9.
Unspecified eating disorder ruled less likely as duration and presentation fit binge-eating disorder or overeating associated with psychological disturbances.
Ruled out F50.4 as overeating is not driven by emotional distress or used as a psychological comfort mechanism.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent episodes of eating objectively large amounts of food with a subjective loss of control ('can't seem to stop once I start'), occurring on average 1–2 nights per week over the past 3 to 5 months. The patient explicitly denies engaging in recurrent inappropriate compensatory behaviors (purging, laxative misuse, fasting, or excessive exercise), ruling out bulimia nervosa. The patient also denies eating primarily to cope with or comfort emotional distress, making F50.8 (binge eating disorder) the most fitting diagnosis.
